statement: Of the small randomised programmes previously listed here as positive signals without adequately sized follow-up, only BMS-986020 has a positive result on a clinical endpoint (FVC), and that programme stopped for drug-related toxicity while a successor molecule in the same pathway is now in phase 3. statement: Bexotegrast is harmful in IPF on the evidence available: an adequately sized randomised phase 2b trial was terminated on DSMB recommendation with more disease-progression events and more deaths on active treatment than on placebo, in both dose arms and in a dose-ordered pattern. In BEACON-IPF (NCT06097260, n=319 randomised), terminated on DSMB recommendation, registry-posted results show more disease-progression events on bexotegrast than placebo: 5 of 106 (placebo), 16 of 105 (160 mg) and 25 of 108 (320 mg); Cox hazard ratios versus placebo 3.31 (95% CI 1.21-9.05, p=0.0194) and 5.36 (95% CI 2.05-13.99, p=0.0006). A >=10% absolute FVC decline was also more frequent (odds ratio 3.33, 95% CI 1.03-10.81, p=0.0449 for 160 mg; 3.01, 95% CI 0.91-9.91, p=0.07 for 320 mg). Deaths: 0 of 106, 6 of 105 and 4 of 108; serious adverse events 6, 17 and 21. The week-52 FVC primary endpoint is uninformative because only 1, 1 and 2 participants reached week 52 after early termination.
subject: bexotegrast (PLN-74809)
outcome_dimension: E2 disease progression / lung function; E7 survival; E4 safety
evidence_tier_sublabel: one adequately sized randomised trial, registry-posted results, terminated early; no peer-reviewed publication of these results identified

statement: Inhaled GB0139 does not slow lung-function decline in IPF. In GALACTIC-1 (NCT03832946, n=172, quadruple-masked, 52 weeks) the annual rate of FVC decline was -316.60 mL/year (95% CI -394.86 to -238.35) on GB0139 3 mg versus -127.41 mL/year (95% CI -221.12 to -33.71) on placebo, with more respiratory hospitalisations (17 of 102 versus 5 of 70) and worse SGRQ change. No between-arm test is posted and the trial is unpublished, so the apparent harm direction is recorded but not graded as harm.
subject: GB0139 (TD139), inhaled galectin-3 inhibitor
evidence_tier_sublabel: one adequately sized randomised trial, registry-posted only
caveat: Registry posting is the only source; no publication, no statistical comparison, and high attrition in both arms. Conflicts register X12.

statement: HZN-825 does not slow lung-function decline in IPF. In NCT05032066 (n=153, triple-masked, 52 weeks) the change in FVC % predicted differed from placebo by -1.13 (95% CI -3.56 to 1.29, p=0.4388) at 300 mg once daily and -0.39 (95% CI -2.86 to 2.09, p=0.7959) at 300 mg twice daily; the sponsor terminated the trial for not meeting primary or key secondary endpoints.
subject: HZN-825 (fipaxalparant), oral LPA1 antagonist
evidence_tier_sublabel: one adequately sized randomised trial, registry-posted only
caveat: Unpublished. Secondary endpoints are internally discordant (worse composite progression on the twice-daily arm, fewer >=10% FVC decliners) - conflicts register X11.

statement: Two further neurokinin- and P2X3-directed antitussives do not reduce IPF cough on their trials' primary endpoints. Orvepitant (NCT05185089, n=80 crossover) differed from placebo by 0.00 (95% CI -0.62 to 0.63, p=0.989) at 10 mg and -0.58 (95% CI -1.16 to 0.01, p=0.054) at 30 mg on daily cough severity. Gefapixant (NCT02502097, published PMID 34152585) showed no significant reduction in awake objective cough frequency at day 14 (p=0.90).
subject: orvepitant; gefapixant
evidence_tier_sublabel: two randomised crossover trials, one published and one registry-posted only
caveat: Both trials are short (2-6 weeks) and small; gefapixant's efficacy analysis excluded 7 of 51 randomised patients after a protocol amendment. This adds to the existing negative cough evidence (cromolyn, thalidomide-era work) rather than opening a new question.

statement: Whether combined autoantibody reduction (therapeutic plasma exchange plus rituximab plus intravenous immunoglobulin) improves survival after an acute exacerbation of IPF is uncertain and untested by any analysable source. STRIVE-IPF (NCT03286556) posts six-month survival of 44% (SE 9, n=33) versus 7% (SE 6, n=18) on treatment as usual, but the trial is open-label, the arms are unequal from 82 enrolled, no baseline lung function or oxygen requirement is posted, no statistical analysis is posted, and no results publication exists. In stable IPF, blinded rituximab monotherapy was null with numerically more hospitalisations.
subject: autoantibody reduction for acute exacerbations of IPF
evidence_tier_sublabel: one open-label randomised trial, registry-posted only, plus uncontrolled pilot data
caveat: A survival difference of this size in an unblinded trial with unposted baseline severity cannot be separated from case selection. Conflicts register X9. The smallest next step is retrieval of the trial's analysis and publication, not a new trial.
phase6_status: added in Phase 6 (C27); held at verification

statement: Five investigational programmes now have IPF randomised data that show no signal of benefit but are too small or too truncated to be decisive: LTP001 (n=46, terminated by sponsor decision, FVC % predicted -3.1 versus -1.1), ianalumab (n=30, terminated, FVC difference 0.063 L, p=0.3248), tanzisertib/CC-90001 (n=112 dosed, terminated on a strategic decision, ppFVC differences 1.1 and 2.2 with confidence intervals spanning zero, PMID 38484130), tipelukast (n=15) and belumosudil (open-label, no comparison posted). These are recorded as uncertain, not as failures.

evidence_tier_sublabel: randomised but underpowered or truncated trials
caveat: Sponsor termination for business reasons is not evidence of inefficacy; equally, an unpowered null is not evidence of efficacy. None of these programmes reaches the threshold for a research lead under the Phase 4 screens.

statement: A single-centre randomised posting claims a 73.2% reduction in daily coughing episodes versus 16.1% on saline placebo over 21 days in 50 IPF patients (difference -57.13, 95% CI -63.99 to -50.27, p=0.0001), together with a 27.9% rise in the FEV1/FVC ratio and zero adverse events in both arms. There is no publication, no described cough-measurement method and no outcomes-assessor masking, and the accompanying values are not consistent with the known behaviour of IPF over three weeks. The claim is recorded as unverified.

section: S5 What we do not know
statement: A distinct class of IPF evidence exists that is neither published nor absent: trial results posted to a registry without a between-arm analysis, without a publication, or both. In this record it covers at least nine entities, including two adequately sized phase 2 trials (GALACTIC-1, n=172; HZN-825, n=153) and the only randomised survival result in acute exacerbations (STRIVE-IPF). Registry postings are primary source material and were graded as such, but where the sponsor posts no analysis and publishes no report, the evidence can be described and not weighed.
subject: results that exist but cannot be graded
evidence_tier_sublabel: fact about the record, not about an intervention
caveat: Rows M5.7-M5.13 are facts about the record's completeness, not about any intervention. The remedy is retrieval, not new trials.

section: S5 What we do not know
statement: The largest single block of randomised IPF evidence that this record has not examined is Chinese-language. English-indexed systematic reviews that searched CNKI, Wanfang, VIP and CBM pool 63 randomised trials of Chinese medicine injections, 23 trials in 1390 patients of qi-supplementing and blood-activating herbs, 20 trials in 1363 patients across four injection products, 11 trials in 981 patients of external TCM treatment, and a herbal-versus-N-acetylcysteine comparison in 733 patients. No injection product and no head-to-head herbal comparison appears in the 279-intervention landscape.
subject: Chinese-language randomised evidence not examined by this record
evidence_tier_sublabel: fact about the record, not about an intervention
caveat: These counts come from secondary sources; the underlying trials were not read and their reviews' own quality statements are cautionary. The counts describe how much evidence exists, not whether any of it shows benefit. No verdict is assigned to any of this evidence.

section: S5 What we do not know
statement: Non-reporting of completed IPF trials is genuine rather than a search artefact. Of 110 completed trials with no retrievable results, a targeted registry-identifier search of PubMed found any indexed publication for only 7, and none of those reported the trial's missing primary clinical outcome: they were design papers, pre-completion reports, or safety, pharmacokinetic and preclinical papers.
subject: unreported completed trials
evidence_tier_sublabel: fact about the record, not about an intervention
caveat: The search covered PubMed only; results could exist in conference abstracts, theses, regulatory dossiers or non-indexed journals. Two entities were added to the landscape as a result, both phase 1 safety and pharmacokinetics only.

statement: The magnitude of corticosteroid harm in IPF is not established, and the direction depends on the setting. The best available synthesis (10 observational studies, 1639 patients with fibrotic ILD) found an uncertain effect on mortality (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.85-1.25) and, in IPF specifically, an uncertain effect on FVC decline (mean difference -3.80% predicted, 95% CI -8.94 to 1.34), both graded very low certainty. In acute exacerbation, one propensity-weighted cohort (n=82, 37 treated) found no association with in-hospital mortality (adjusted HR 1.31) alongside worse overall survival (HR 6.17); a second cohort (n=238) found pulse dosing no better than non-pulse; a third (n=153 and n=229) found early dose tapering associated with better survival (IPW-adjusted HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.14-0.99 and 0.27, 95% CI 0.094-0.83).
subject: systemic corticosteroids (monotherapy, excluding the PANTHER triple-therapy regimen)
evidence_tier_sublabel: observational evidence only, graded very low certainty by its own authors; confounding by indication is not resolved
caveat: None of these studies can separate a corticosteroid effect from the severity that prompted the prescription. The record's separate finding of harm from prednisone plus azathioprine plus N-acetylcysteine (PANTHER-IPF) is randomised evidence about a three-drug regimen and does not transfer to corticosteroid monotherapy. The tapering result is about how long steroids are continued, not whether they help.

section: S5 What we do not know
statement: FVC is a validated prognostic marker in IPF but has not been validated as a treatment-effect surrogate. Patient-level evidence is strong: in pooled nintedanib trial data (n=2583) a faster rate of FVC decline and a lower current FVC each predicted death over 52 weeks (HR 1.79, 95% CI 1.57-2.03 and HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.17-1.32 per 5-percentage-point decrease), and in a prospective registry, adjusted declines of at least 2%, 5% and 10% predicted were associated with 1.8-, 2.3- and 2.7-fold increases in the risk of death or transplantation. What no published analysis establishes is the trial-level question: whether a drug's effect on FVC predicts its effect on survival.
subject: FVC as a surrogate endpoint
outcome_dimension: surrogacy of the record's primary outcome measure
evidence_tier_sublabel: fact about the record's outcome measure, not about an intervention
caveat: Patient-level prognostic association is not surrogacy. Every 'slows progression' verdict in this record rests on FVC, so this gap propagates to those verdicts: it does not make them wrong, but it means the survival consequence of the observed FVC benefit is inferred rather than measured. Individual IPF trials are underpowered for mortality, so the trial-level analysis is unlikely to be informative without pooled individual participant data.
